Tools

Family Map: Where Everything Is

When an emergency, illness or death happens, families often lose days searching for policies, deeds and contacts. This sheet puts in one place where everything is and whom to call. Fill it in by hand, update it once a year and keep it somewhere secure that trusted people know about.

Treat this sheet as a confidential document. Do not write account numbers, passwords, Social Security numbers or access codes. Keep it somewhere secure, share it only with trusted people and destroy old versions when you update it. It is designed to be printed and filled in by hand.

Policies

Include policies for every property and entity (LLCs, trusts). Also note each company's claims phone number.

Type (home, flood, auto, umbrella, life, etc.)CompanyPolicy numberAgent and phoneExpiration

Properties and deeds

Note who holds title to each property: the owner should match the named insured on the policy.

Property or addressOwner (person, LLC or trust)Where the deed isMortgage or lenderNotes

Vehicles and boats

For boats, also note the marina, the contract and where the hurricane plan is kept.

Type (car, boat, aircraft)Description and yearOwnerWhere the title or registration isRelated policy

Collections and appraisals

Note where the photo and video inventory is, such as the cloud folder, without writing the password here.

Category (jewelry, art, watches, wine)DescriptionDate of last appraisalAppraiser and contactWhere the appraisal is kept

Accounts and advisors

Names and contacts only. Do not write account numbers, passwords, access codes or security answers on this sheet.

Role (bank, CPA, attorney, financial advisor)NameFirm or institutionPhone or email

Household staff

Note whether workers' compensation or employment practices coverage is in place and where the work agreement is kept.

NameRolePhoneStart dateRelated coverage or documents

Emergency contacts

Include at least one contact who lives outside Florida, which helps during a hurricane.

NameRelationshipPhoneHas a key or access?

Where the originals are kept

If you use a safe deposit box, note which institution holds it and who is authorized to open it.

Document (will, trust, powers of attorney, passports, titles)Where it isWho has accessDigital copy? (yes or no)

Where does your family stand on this?

The Family Protection Map takes three minutes, is anonymous, and shows which parts of your plan are still blank.
